resolutions.researcher_notes: Searched hard, no source states $760,000,000 for this pipeline specifically. Ruled out: (1) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects historical database has no NET Mexico row at all (checked both 'Historical Projects' sheets); (2) both seed IJGlobal transaction pages (ijglobal.com/data/transaction/28108 and /36270, the type of source that would normally carry a project-finance total-cost figure) are Cloudflare-blocked ('Attention Required') and confirmed via the Wayback availability API (archive.org/wayback/available) to have ZERO captures for either URL -- a genuine access dead end, not a substitute-with-snapshot case; (3) hydrocarbons-technology.com's project page (live host redirects/403s, but its Wayback capture from 2024-05-29 is readable) states 'Estimated Investment $665m' for the whole NET Mexico project -- close in order of magnitude but does not match $760M, and using it would misrepresent a $665m estimate as support for a $760,000,000 sheet value, which the brief's no-orphan-ref rule forbids; (4) the 2015 PR Newswire acquisition-completion release and NextEra's related 8-Ks state only portfolio-level figures for the whole NET Midstream acquisition (a ~$2.1 billion transaction: ~$934 million cash plus ~$654 million assumed debt plus deferred/contingent payments) that do not decompose into a discrete $760M figure for the NET Mexico pipeline alone; (5) checked NextEra Energy Partners' Sept. 2015 424B5 prospectus supplement (SEC accession 0001193125-15-316539) full text for cost language near every mention of 'NET Mexico' -- found only a $100 million aggregate expansion-capex figure (covering NET Mexico, Eagle Ford and Monument pipelines together, not $760M) and an unrelated $710-760 million *partnership-wide 2016 EBITDA guidance range* (a coincidental match on the digits '760' with no connection to construction/acquisition cost); (6) SEC EDGAR full-text search for '"NET Mexico" "$760"' and similar combinations returned no filing tying $760 million to this pipeline. Leaving UNRESOLVED per the brief's rule against proposing a ref that doesn't actually support the value, rather than citing the closest-but-non-matching $665m estimate.

NextEra Energy Partners' 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (filed 2015-11-06) states verbatim: 'NET Mexico is owned 90% by NET Mexico Pipeline, LP[,] the Managing Member, and 10% by MGI Enterprises US LLC ("MGI"), a Member and indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Pemex Gas y Petroquimica Basica' -- an exact match to the sheet's Owner1=NextEra Energy 90.00% / Owner2=MGI Enterprises 10.00% (NET Mexico Pipeline, LP was NEP's/NextEra's holding vehicle for its interest). PEMEX's own 2013 Form F-4 Exhibit 21.1 (filer: Mexican Petroleum et al., a wholly independent second publisher) separately lists 'MGI Enterprises, Limited' among Pemex Gas y Petroquimica Basica's own 100%-owned subsidiaries -- this corroborates MGI Enterprises' identity/parentage (a genuine Pemex-family entity) from a source with no relationship to NextEra, but it does not itself state the specific 90/10 NET Mexico split, so it is not counted toward independence of the OWNERSHIP-PERCENTAGE claim, only cited as supporting identity corroboration. Both the 90/10 split figure and the 2013 PEMEX filing are single-origin per claim, hence medium/independent:false rather than high. CONCERN (informational only, no value changed): the ownership described by the sheet is NO LONGER CURRENT. NextEra Energy Partners' own Q3 2023 10-Q (Exhibit, SEC accession 0001603145-23-000046, 'nep-q32023xex21.htm', filed 2023-11-07) is itself the Stock/Membership-Interest Purchase Agreement under which NEP's subsidiary NEP DC Holdings sold its interests in 'NET Mexico Pipeline Partners, LLC' (together with the Dos Caminos and EFM systems) to a buyer -- the agreement again names MGI Enterprises' 10% stake as continuing ('MGI Interests... represent ten percent (10%) of the aggregate issued and outstanding Equity Interests in NET Mexico', held constant through the sale). Kinder Morgan, Inc.'s FY2024 Form 10-K Exhibit 21.1 (filed 2025-02-13) confirms the buyer: it lists 'NET Mexico Pipeline Partners, LLC (90%)' as a KMI subsidiary. Together, two independent SEC-reporting companies (NextEra Energy Partners as seller, Kinder Morgan as buyer/current parent) confirm that ownership of the 90% interest passed from NextEra to Kinder Morgan around Q3-Q4 2023, with MGI Enterprises' 10% unchanged throughout. The value AS CURRENTLY WRITTEN on the sheet (NextEra Energy 90% / MGI Enterprises 10%) is well-documented and accurate for the 2015-2023 period and is what this ref unit supports; a human should consider whether Owner1 should be updated to Kinder Morgan to reflect the post-2023 sale, per the brief's rule not to change values from a citation-gap pass.
